rounds.text: Chennai Petroleum Corporation Ltd is currently trading at a highly attractive valuation, with a P/E ratio of 4.72x [E1] that sits significantly below the sector benchmark of 15.54x [E6]. This undervaluation is underscored by an EV/EBITDA of 3.26x, which is less than half of the sector's 7.86x benchmark [E11]. The company demonstrates exceptional capital efficiency, evidenced by an ROE of 31.8% [E13] and an ROCE of 34.9% [E12], both of which vastly outperform their respective sector benchmarks [E9, E10]. Furthermore, the company is in a robust financial position with a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.18x [E38] and a strong cash-generating ability, producing Rs 2,045 Cr in free cash flow as of March 2026 [E36]. Conceded: the company has experienced negative compounded sales growth of -6% and profit growth of -5% over the last three years [E16, E20], and the yearly operating-margin trend remains inconsistent [E32]. Despite these fluctuations, the company achieved a record crude throughput of 112% of installed capacity [E88] and is actively investing in future growth through a Rs 2,000 crore capital expenditure plan for retail and LOBS projects [E83, E98].

Management expects the momentum of resilient operational and financial performance to continue in the new financial year.
evidence.quote: To summarize, we continue to deliver resilient operational and financial performance and see the momentum to continue in the new financial year as well.

evidence.fact: The company expects to see significant commissioning of retail outlets in the 2026-27 financial year.
evidence.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started. And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

evidence.fact: Management expects higher throughput in FY26 compared to the previous year due to a lower impact from maintenance shutdowns.
evidence.quote: Now, when you look forward 2025-26, the impact of shutdown that will happen in the current year is lower than that in the previous year. There is one unit shutdown, one primary unit. If you make a single index, it will be lower than what happened last year. So, you can expect a throughput which is higher than last year on the operational part.

evidence.fact: Management believes net GRMs or net cracks for diesel and ATF are currently close to long-term averages.
evidence.quote: When I'm speaking, that is today, when I compare today's net GRM or net cracks to that way, I find them to be close to the long-term average.

evidence.fact: The company considers $13 per barrel to be the long-term average for GRM.
evidence.quote: I found around 13 $/bbl to be the long-term average.

evidence.fact: India's petroleum product demand is experiencing sustained growth driven by urbanization, industrialization, and infrastructure development.
evidence.quote: India continues to be among the fastest-growing major economies in the world, with rising urbanization, industrialization and infrastructure development driving sustained growth in petroleum product demand.

evidence.fact: The company is executing a Group 2 and Group 3 LOBS project with an estimated cost of INR 1,600 crores.
evidence.quote: LOBS project, Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project is INR1,600 crores.

evidence.fact: CPCL has ventured into a retail outlet project with an estimated investment of INR 400 crores.
evidence.quote: The retail outlet project is INR400 crores. So that makes it INR2,000 crores. This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years.

evidence.fact: The company plans for a normal annual maintenance capex of approximately INR 500 crores.
evidence.quote: Besides, every year, you can assume another INR500 crores is our normal capex.

evidence.fact: The gross refining margin for FY 2025-26 was $9.2 per barrel compared to the Singapore benchmark of $5.83.
evidence.quote: The gross refining margin, GRM, for financial year 2025- '26 was $9.2 per barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $5.83 per barrel.

evidence.fact: The core GRM for the fourth quarter was $10.3 per barrel.
evidence.quote: 10.3 $/bbl would be the core GRM.

evidence.fact: Niche products like MTO and Hexane contribute approximately 15% of the company's margins.
evidence.quote: About 7% to 8% constitutes these kinds of niche products. And this 7%–8% is currently contributing around 15% of my margins.

evidence.fact: CPCL achieved a record crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, representing 112% of installed capacity.
evidence.quote: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, million metric ton, which equivalents to 112% of installed capacity, breaking records of our previous best of 11.64 MMT achieved in financial year 2023-'24.

evidence.fact: The company processed 52% high sulphur crude during the financial year.
evidence.quote: During the financial year, we processed 52% high sulphur.

evidence.fact: CPCL has secured 55% to 60% of its crude requirements through long-term agreements.
evidence.quote: Due to our flexible crude-sourcing mechanism, we have strategically secured 55% to 60% through long-term agreements, the remaining on short-term basis from diverse sources

evidence.fact: The company's net debt-to-equity ratio stands at 0.09.
evidence.quote: If we consider net borrowing, the debt ratio is only 0.09, which is less than 0.1.

evidence.fact: The Board recommended a total dividend of INR 62 per share for the year, including an interim dividend.
evidence.quote: the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR54 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR62 per share, which again is highest ever.

evidence.fact: Net borrowings for the company are currently INR 973 crores.
evidence.quote: On a gross basis, the borrowings are INR1,900 crores, but on a net basis, it is less than INR1,000 crores, to be precise, INR973 crores.

evidence.fact: Geopolitical events and logistical constraints pose challenges and drive volatility in crude oil prices.
evidence.quote: Now with all this, I would like to say the uncertainties due to logistical constraints, volatility of crude oil prices do pose challenges.

evidence.fact: Foreign exchange losses for the financial year amounted to approximately INR 350 crores.
evidence.quote: And for the whole year, it will be around INR350 crores.

evidence.fact: The company observed a 30% to 40% disturbance in Middle East cargo flows over a short period.
evidence.quote: What has impacted is that maybe 30% to 40% was affected over a very short period, but all have assured us that depending on the situation, they will make up all the cargoes.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (FY27): The company will see a lot of commissioning of retail outlets during the current financial year.
evidence.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started. And this year, that is '26-'27, we'll see a lot of commissioning out of them.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (next 2 years): The company plans to spend INR 2,000 crores on LOBS and retail outlet projects over the coming years.
evidence.quote: The retail outlet project is INR400 crores. So that makes it INR2,000 crores. This INR2,000 crores will happen over 2 to 3 years.

evidence.fact: Management commitment: The company has a scheduled maintenance and inspection of one of its refinery units.
evidence.quote: But yes, maybe close to September, October, we have a scheduled M&I of one of our refinery units.
